data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2023 were GBP 144.4m. During 2023 the syndicate's gross reserves reduced to GBP 60.4m at 31 December 2023, reflecting a combination of reinsurance to close activity and movements in claims provisions. Analysis of the claims development table shows a modest favourable prior-year development of c. GBP 2.5m (a ~1.7% release relative to opening reserves) attributable primarily to favourable emergence in longer-tail and Specialty classes. Primary drivers cited are favourable claims development in longer-tail lines and Specialty classes; notable prior-year loss events (e.g. Hurricane Ida, Winterstorm Uri, European and Australian floods and the Ukraine-related losses) remain referenced but were not quantified in the prior-year movement figure.
raw_causal_phrases: The Syndicate has also seen improvement in its prior year reserves for 2022 & 2021, due to good experience on its longer tail and Specialty classes.
However, the Syndicate's narrowly defined risk appetite has seen limited impact from these events through the year.
data.data_quality_notes: Opening reserves taken from Statement of Financial Position (claims outstanding, gross) at 1 Jan 2023 (prior year column). Prior-year development derived from the gross claims development table (triangle) by excluding 2023 and 2022 columns and comparing the 2021 current estimate to its previous diagonal (release of GBP 2.5m). There is an External RITC amount (61.6) shown in technical provisions which materially affects the gross balances and may distort simple trend comparisons; where possible the triangle was used to isolate prior-year movement. Some events are mentioned narratively without quantified gross impacts; net figures are not used except where RDS provides syndicate-share estimates. Confidence levels reflect whether figures are explicit (1.0), calculated from printed tables (0.8) or inferred (0.5-0.6).
